samples.summary: New `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH = 32` duplicates the existing `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32` (`packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:111`), which caps the very same thing — nested-table recursion over a docs `Block` tree — in the same package. Neither constant references the other, so nothing records that they must agree: `bandBlockNumerics` stops banding numeric attributes at `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH`, and if the new reader cap were ever raised above it, readers would materialize tables whose peer-written `fontSize`/`padding`/`rowHeight` were never banded and feed them straight to `computeTableLayout` — the exact hazard `docs/design/docs/docs.md:290-298` says the band exists to close. Reuse (or at minimum a documented `{@link}` between the two) was available inside one package.

`hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` / `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` (backend) and `hasTableAtNestingCap` (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:452`) are byte-for-byte the same predicate over the shared `@wafflebase/docs` `Block`/`Document` model, with no CRDT specifics in either. The constant they test against is already exported from `@wafflebase/docs` (`src/index.ts:97`, `src/node.ts:145`), so the predicate could have shipped next to it and been imported by both. As two copies they are two answers to one question: if the counting convention changes on one side, the backend `PUT`/copy paths and the editor will disagree about which documents are writable.

`capTableNesting` / `capTableCellsNesting` are pure model transformations (walk `Block[]`/`TableCell[][]`, drop tables past a depth) filed in the `view/` clipboard module. Their natural home is beside `model/table-nesting.ts` with the constant and `Doc.tableNestingDepth`; as it stands the only other producer that needs the identical operation — the DOCX importer (`src/import/docx-importer.ts:437`) — reimplements the cap inline rather than reusing them, and any future non-view producer (CLI import, backend) cannot reach them without importing from the view layer.

Scope: a bug fix for #1049 (nested-table cell rectangles, shift+click parity, copy) is bundled with a ~20-file hardening program that reverses a stated design Goal ("Recursive nesting with no hard depth limit" → a hard 32-level ceiling) and adds three further independent mechanisms — `blockParentMap` cycle guards in seven walks, a `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` budget that splits `expandCellRangeForMerges` into exact/budgeted modes, and clamping of peer-written `tableCellRange` indices. Each is defensible on its own, but none of them is required to make the nested-table selection work, and a Goal reversal in particular is the kind of decision that deserves its own change so it can be accepted or rejected independently of the bug fix.

`rest-api.md` is the canonical doc for `PUT /content` and enumerates its validation contract, including the depth bound (`MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH`, 32). This change alters that contract for docs bodies — the block walk now rejects at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` instead of `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (`packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:454`), a new class of 400 for API consumers — and the new behaviour is recorded only in `docs-nested-tables.md` §7. The endpoint's own doc should carry it.

`DocumentCopyService` gains a new user-visible refusal (copy fails with a 400 when the source holds a table at the nesting cap), but `document-copy.md`'s "Failure handling" section — which explicitly enumerates the copy's failure modes down to "a type with no arm above is a 400" — is not updated. The behaviour is described only in `docs-nested-tables.md`, i.e. in a doc a reader of the copy feature has no reason to open.

Two architectural decisions on the presence render path are undocumented: peer-supplied `tableCellRange` indices are now clamped to the resolved table in `normalizeCellRange`, and `expandCellRangeForMerges` grows a budgeted mode (`MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS`) used only by `computeSelectionRects`, so the same function now returns an exact answer for callers that write and a possibly-short one for the painter. `docs-presence.md` defines the `tableCellRange` presence payload and is the natural place to record that it is untrusted input with a bounded consumer; neither it nor `docs-tables.md` mentions the split.

The interactive "insert table in cell" command at the ceiling simply `return`s with no user-visible feedback, so the gesture appears to do nothing; the design doc says only that it "refuses at the ceiling" without stating what the user sees. Other refusals in this change surface as errors; this one is silent.
